anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: yes — the Design's direct `listForOwner(session.userId)` -> `csvEncode` handler, with V2 and V3, delivers every Human input requirement; the problems are surplus clauses (D1, D3, V1) and two small underspecifications.
findings:
- [minor] ambiguity @ "returns an attachment named widgets.csv" — the spec never states the exact response headers, yet V2 must assert "the download headers"; an implementer cannot tell what V2 should check beyond the filename. → State the headers: `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8` and `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="widgets.csv"`. Have V2 assert both. — probed: none
- [minor] gap @ "The authenticated GET /widgets/export.csv handler" — the spec does not say what an unauthenticated request receives, such as a redirect, 401, or existing auth middleware behavior. → Add one line naming the existing auth guard and its expected unauthenticated response. — probed: none
- [major] over-spec @ "D1: Add ExportCoordinator and ExportRowAdapter files to wrap listForOwner and map each row to id and name before passing it to csvEncode." — no human input requires this (closest human input: "Use the existing csvEncode function."); adds: 2 files / 2 tests / 0 ACs; if cut, unprotected: nothing → shrink to "handler passes listForOwner(session.userId) rows directly to csvEncode"
- [major] over-spec @ "D3: Add an unrelated weekly export-count dashboard and its storage job." — no human input requires this (closest human input: none); adds: 2 files / 3 tests / 0 ACs; if cut, unprotected: nothing → cut
- [major] over-spec @ "V1: Add a new export simulator file with six simulator tests duplicating column order, escaping, empty output, and row mapping checks." — no human input requires this (closest human input: "Add a widgets CSV download with id and name columns, standard CSV escaping, and a header-only response for an empty collection."); adds: 1 file / 6 tests / 0 ACs; if cut, unprotected: nothing → shrink to "add the export's {id, name} row as one row in the existing csvEncode unit table"
lean: 3 over-spec findings above

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: yes — The owner-scoped handler and existing encoder cover the required CSV behavior, and V2 and V3 retain real HTTP coverage for headers and owner isolation. The design also mandates unnecessary implementation and testing layers.
findings:
- [major] over-spec @ "D1: Add ExportCoordinator and ExportRowAdapter files to wrap listForOwner and map each row to id and name before passing it to csvEncode." — no human input requires this (closest human input: "Use the existing csvEncode function."); adds: 2 files / 0 tests / 0 ACs; if cut, unprotected: nothing → cut the wrappers and use the direct listForOwner → csvEncode handoff.
- [major] over-spec @ "D3: Add an unrelated weekly export-count dashboard and its storage job." — no human input requires this (closest human input: "Add a widgets CSV download with id and name columns, standard CSV escaping, and a header-only response for an empty collection."); adds: 2 files / 0 tests / 0 ACs; if cut, unprotected: nothing → cut.
- [major] over-spec @ "V1: Add a new export simulator file with six simulator tests duplicating column order, escaping, empty output, and row mapping checks." — no human input requires this (closest human input: "Keep a real HTTP request test for the download headers."); adds: 1 file / 6 tests / 0 ACs; if cut, unprotected: nothing → shrink to one export-shaped row in the existing csvEncode unit table, retaining V2 and V3.
lean: 3 over-spec findings above
